## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Restore the empty-criteria guard in `requirement_proven` before merge: right now a requirement with no criteria counts as proven, even though the pull request says no behavior change is intended.

## Changes
The pull request replaces `typing.List`/`Dict` with built-in generics and `log.warn` with `log.warning` across 180 `h*_records.py` handlers and `h091_requirements.py`. It switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`, rewrites `requirement_proven` to compare a sum against `len(criteria)`, and adds a one-line `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Return False again when criteria is empty — With `criteria=[]`, `requirement_proven` now returns `True` because `sum(...) == len(criteria)` is `0 == 0`. The removed `bool(criteria) and all(...)` returned `False`. The warning on line 10 is logged, but execution then continues into the success result. `test_requirement_proof` never passes an empty list. — Release review now treats a requirement with no criteria as proven, so unverified requirements pass the gate. — Fix: Restore `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` and add an empty-list assertion to `test_requirement_proof`.

(none)

(none)
